source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: Which record is the fundamental building block of the Field Health Services Information System (FHSIS)?
questions.rationale: The Family Treatment Record is the fundamental building block of FHSIS. The Target Client List is the second building block. Reporting forms are the only routine way data move between facilities.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, FHSIS (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: Fundamental building block of FHSIS

questions.subject: NP I
questions.topic: Care of the Community: Health System, PHC, Epidemiology & Disaster
questions.stem: In FHSIS, what is the ONLY mechanism by which data are routinely sent from one facility to another?
questions.rationale: Reporting forms, prepared monthly or quarterly, are the only mechanism through which FHSIS data are routinely transmitted between facilities.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, FHSIS (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: Only mechanism through which data are routinely transmitted from one facility to another

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Aling Rosa, 24, G2P1, comes to the barangay health station at 16 weeks. She had 2 tetanus toxoid doses in her first pregnancy 2 years ago.
questions.stem: Aling Rosa gets her third tetanus toxoid dose today. How long does TT3 protect her?
questions.rationale: TT2 (4 weeks after TT1) gives 80% protection for 3 years. TT3 (6 months after TT2) gives 95% protection for 5 years. TT4 gives 10 years and TT5 lifetime.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Maternal Health Program (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: TT 3 After 6 months 95% 5 years

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Aling Rosa, 24, G2P1, comes to the barangay health station at 16 weeks. She had 2 tetanus toxoid doses in her first pregnancy 2 years ago.
questions.stem: Which tetanus toxoid dose gives Aling Rosa LIFETIME protection?
questions.rationale: TT5, given 1 year after TT4, gives 99% protection for life.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Maternal Health Program (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: TT 5 After 1 year 99% Lifetime

questions.subject: NP I
questions.situation: Aling Rosa, 24, G2P1, comes to the barangay health station at 16 weeks. She had 2 tetanus toxoid doses in her first pregnancy 2 years ago.
questions.stem: Which iron/folic acid supplement does the nurse give Aling Rosa?
questions.rationale: Pregnant women receive a 60 mg iron/400 mcg folic acid tablet daily, continued up to 2 months postpartum.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Micronutrient Supplementation (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: Iron/Folic acid 60mg/400ug tablet Daily

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: During FP counseling, what birth spacing interval does the nurse recommend?
questions.rationale: Family planning counseling in the maternal health program promotes proper spacing of births at 3- to 5-year intervals.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Maternal Health Program (PDF p. 88)
questions.quote: Proper spacing of birth (3 to 5 years interval)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A man had a vasectomy last week. What should the nurse tell him about its effectiveness?
questions.rationale: Vasectomy is very effective 3 months after the procedure, so another method is used until then. He keeps sexual ability and ejaculation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 89)
questions.quote: Very effective in 3 months after the procedure

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A breastfeeding mother wants to use the Lactational Amenorrhea Method. For how long is LAM effective at most?
questions.rationale: LAM is a temporary postpartum method effective for a maximum of 6 months. It depends on full or nearly full breastfeeding.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 90)
questions.quote: Short term FP method which is effective only for a maximum of 6 months

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which FP method encourages male participation and protects against sexually transmitted infections?
questions.rationale: The male condom has no hormonal effect, protects against microorganisms during intercourse, and encourages male participation in family planning.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 90)
questions.quote: Encourages male participation in family planning

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which family planning method uses color-coded cycle beads?
questions.rationale: In the Standard Days Method, couples use color-coded cycle beads to mark fertile and infertile days. It suits women whose cycles are usually 26 to 32 days long.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 91)
questions.quote: Couples use color coded cycle beads to mark the fertile and infertile days of the menstrual cycle

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which method identifies fertile days by combining cervical mucus, basal body temperature, and other signs of ovulation?
questions.rationale: The sympto-thermal method combines observations of cervical mucus, basal body temperature, and other ovulation signs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 90)
questions.quote: combination of observations made on the cervical mucus, basal body temperature recording and other signs of ovulation

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A woman says family planning will make her sterile. How should the nurse view this belief?
questions.rationale: Common FP misconceptions include that FP causes abortion, makes couples sterile, or causes loss of sexual desire. The nurse corrects these through counseling.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Family Planning (PDF p. 91)
questions.quote: Will render couples sterile

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which is a key IYCF message the nurse teaches a new mother?
questions.rationale: Key IYCF messages: initiate breastfeeding within 1 hour after birth, breastfeed exclusively for 6 months, add complementary food at 6 months, and continue to 2 years and beyond.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Infant & Young Child Feeding (PDF p. 91)
questions.quote: Initiate breastfeeding within 1hour after birth

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A mother gives her 3-month-old breast milk plus a little water on hot days. Is this exclusive breastfeeding?
options: No, only breast milk is given
Yes, if under 30 mL a day
questions.rationale: Exclusive breastfeeding means giving only breast milk, with no other liquids or solids, not even water.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Infant & Young Child Feeding (PDF p. 91)
questions.quote: Exclusive breastfeeding means giving a baby only breast milk, and no other liquids or solids, not even water.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which law promotes rooming-in and protects and supports breastfeeding in health facilities?
questions.rationale: The Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Act of 1992 (RA 7600) promotes rooming-in and protects and supports breastfeeding. Mother and baby stay together 24 hours.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Laws that Protect IYCF (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Act of 1992 (RA 7600)

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: The Food Fortification Law (RA 8976) requires mandatory fortification of which staple foods?
questions.rationale: RA 8976 mandates fortification of rice, flour, edible oil, and sugar, with voluntary fortification of processed foods.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Laws that Protect IYCF (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: mandatory food fortification of staple foods – rice, flour, edible oil and sugar

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A child missed his second pentavalent dose by 2 months. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The vaccine schedule is not restarted, and no extra dose is given to a child who missed a dose. The nurse continues with the next dose.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Principles (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: No extra must be given to children/ mother who missed a dose

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which statement about giving several EPI vaccines on one day is correct?
options: Give them all at one site
questions.rationale: It is safe and effective to give all EPI vaccines on the same day at different sites.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Principles (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: It is safe and immunologically effective to administer all EPI vaccines on the same day at different sites of the body

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A child due for vaccines has a mild cough and low-grade fever. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: Malnutrition, low-grade fever, mild respiratory infection, cough, diarrhea, and vomiting are false contraindications.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, False Contraindications (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: False Contraindications

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: Which is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to the next DPT-containing dose?
questions.rationale: DPT2 or DPT3 is not given to a child who had convulsions or shock within 3 days of the previous dose.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Absolute Contraindications (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: DPT 2 or DPT 3 to a child who has had convulsions or shock within 3 days the previous dose.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: For which child is BCG contraindicated?
questions.rationale: Live vaccines such as BCG must not be given to people immunosuppressed by malignant disease. The others are false contraindications.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Absolute Contraindications (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: Live vaccines like BCG vaccine must not be given to individuals who are immunosuppressed due to a malignant disease.

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: How should the nurse reconstitute freeze-dried vaccines?
options: Only the diluent supplied with it
questions.rationale: EPI strictly follows the principle of never reconstituting freeze-dried vaccines with anything other than the diluent supplied.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, EPI Principles (PDF p. 92)
questions.quote: never, ever reconstituting the freeze dried vaccines other than the diluents supplied
